title: Layered wave-pinning crawlers from a random field: 31-33 random domains coarsen into round cells that each make their own layer, self-polarize into half-moon crawlers and absorb static cells on contact (seeds 0-1)
summary: world.py = the claim world of 20261026T0243-c31-crawler-layer-repair-claim (layer made by the polarity protein, excluded cargo) started from an unstructured field: a smoothed white-noise field thresholded at area fraction 0.3 (31-33 random domains over the whole box), rho = 1 +- 0.2 uniform noise inside, protein 2.64 per unit area, per-body pools, and a cap of 2.5 on each body's cytosolic concentration (without it, protein in vanishing fragments diverges and the run blows up). On seeds 0 and 1 (snap.py, t=0-12): curvature flow and the polarity's area window leave 6-8 round cells by t=2, each with its own s ring (layer s row); the larger ones break symmetry by themselves (as in c22's uniformly polarized disk) and crawl as half-moons, and a crawler that touches a static disk absorbs it, so 3 bodies remain at t=6 and 1-2 crawlers at t=12 (noise_s0.png, noise_s1.png). Labkit packs are running.
